exercises.question: Create a job tracker with fields for eligibility, role fit, application date, follow-up and status.
exercises.answer: Tracker fields: employer, role, vacancy URL, date captured, location eligibility, essential requirements, role-fit score, evidence gap, application date, resume version, contact, stage, next action/date, interview feedback and outcome. Record only legitimate public vacancy information and minimal personal notes. Review weekly and close stale vacancies. Track conversion rates cautiously; small samples do not support strong conclusions.

exercises.question: Research two healthcare analytics employers and summarise their products, data context and likely analyst tasks.
exercises.answer: For each employer, use official company pages, product documentation, annual reports or credible public material. Summarise services, care setting, data types likely used, analyst teams/roles, governance context and possible metrics. Label inferred analyst tasks as hypotheses, not facts. Do not imply access to internal systems or confidential information. Record source URLs and access date.

exercises.question: Write a tailored application plan for a remote entry-level analyst vacancy.
exercises.answer: Plan: confirm location/work-authorisation eligibility; map each essential requirement to evidence; tailor resume and project links; write a concise application note; verify the employer and recruiter; submit through the official channel; record date and follow-up; prepare role-specific SQL, spreadsheet and healthcare case practice. If an essential requirement is absent, decide whether it is a genuine gate or a learnable preference before applying.

exercises.question: Audit a suspicious job offer and list independent verification steps.
exercises.answer: Audit domain spelling, recruiter identity, job presence on official careers site, interview process, salary realism, contract and payment terms, data requests and software installation. Contact the employer using a phone/email independently obtained from its official site. Do not pay fees, deposit cheques, share OTPs or provide bank credentials. Preserve evidence and report suspected fraud to the platform and relevant authorities.

title: First 30/60/90 days
learning_outcomes: Plan a structured first 90 days in a new analytics role.
Map stakeholders, data assets, access controls and business definitions.
Deliver a safe early win without bypassing governance.
Establish quality checks and communication routines.
Build a learning plan based on team priorities and feedback.

blocks.text: Learn the business, team responsibilities, data architecture, metric definitions, access rules, security policy and change process. Meet data owners and stakeholders. Do not assume undocumented definitions.
Reproduce an existing report, validate a dataset, document a recurring process or resolve a bounded data-quality issue. Review changes with the owner and record acceptance.
Take responsibility for a defined dashboard, query, quality check or analysis with documented requirements, testing, handoff and stakeholder feedback.
Identify requester, decision-maker, data owner, technical owner, privacy/security contact and users. Clarify who approves access, metric definitions and release.
Agree on quality, timeliness, communication and documentation expectations. Ask for feedback early and maintain a learning log. Avoid changing production pipelines without review.

exercises.question: Write a 30/60/90-day plan for a junior healthcare data analyst joining a hospital analytics team.
exercises.answer: Days 1–30: understand team, data access, definitions, privacy and recurring reports; reproduce one existing report under supervision. Days 31–60: own a bounded data-quality or SQL deliverable with documented tests. Days 61–90: improve a workflow, present findings and agree next-quarter goals. Each phase needs deliverables, reviewer sign-off and learning objectives. Do not promise production changes before access and governance approvals.

exercises.question: Create a stakeholder and data-access map with approval responsibilities.
exercises.answer: Map data owner, system owner, analyst, clinical/domain reviewer, privacy officer, security/IT, approver and report consumers. For each dataset record purpose, minimum fields, lawful/approved access, refresh, retention, permitted environment and escalation path. Analysts should not grant themselves access or repurpose data beyond the approved purpose. Document approval evidence before extraction.

exercises.question: Design acceptance tests for a recurring monthly medication-utilisation report.
exercises.answer: Acceptance tests for a monthly medication-utilisation report: extract period boundaries inclusive/exclusive as defined; unique patient and order keys; duplicate checks; medication coding coverage; denominator reconciliation to source; missing department and date rates; totals by class reconcile to overall totals; trend comparison to prior period; suppression rules; reproducible rerun and reviewer sign-off. Store test results with report version.

exercises.question: Draft a first-month update that communicates completed work, risks and next steps.
exercises.answer: A first-month update should list onboarding completed, data sources and definitions understood, access still pending, report reproduced, quality issues identified, decisions needed and next month's deliverables. Quantify work only where verified. Explain risks and owners without exposing sensitive records. Ask for feedback on priorities and confirm acceptance criteria for the next assignment.

title: Professional ethics and regulation
learning_outcomes: Apply data minimisation, confidentiality and least-privilege principles.
Distinguish legal frameworks by jurisdiction and organisational context.
Recognise that de-identification and pseudonymisation do not remove every risk.
Escalate privacy incidents and uncertain data-use permissions.
Document ethical limits and avoid unauthorised clinical use.

blocks.text: Collect only what is necessary, for a defined purpose, with appropriate authority and safeguards. Limit access, log use, protect transfers and follow retention and deletion rules.

India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 establishes a framework for digital personal data processing, with commencement, rules and obligations subject to official notifications and applicable dates. Analysts must follow current organisational legal guidance; this chapter is not legal advice.

HIPAA applies to covered entities and business associates in defined US contexts, not automatically to every health dataset worldwide. GDPR applies based on its territorial and material scope. Do not assume one framework substitutes for another.

Removing names is insufficient. Dates, rare conditions, geography, free text and linkable datasets may identify people. Pseudonymised data can remain personal data. Use approved methods and environment-specific controls.

Do not access records out of curiosity, export data without approval, or place PHI in public AI tools. If data are exposed or misdirected, stop further sharing, preserve relevant facts and notify the designated security/privacy contact promptly.

exercises.question: Classify five data-use scenarios as permitted, prohibited or requiring privacy/legal review, with reasons.
exercises.answer: Classify scenarios with rationale: approved minimum-necessary synthetic analysis—permitted under project rules; identifiable data sent to a public chatbot—prohibited; linkage of datasets without approval—requires privacy/legal review and should not proceed; small-cell publication—requires disclosure-risk review; use of approved de-identified data within authorised environment—permitted only within stated purpose and controls. The classification depends on jurisdiction, contracts and organisational policy; escalate uncertain cases.

exercises.question: Create a minimum-necessary data request for a synthetic readmission analysis.
exercises.answer: A minimum-necessary request states purpose, approved cohort, required fields and granularity, date range, intended outputs, access roles, environment, retention/deletion, linkage need and safeguards. Exclude direct identifiers unless explicitly justified and approved. Ask for aggregated or pseudonymised fields where sufficient. Document approvals and never collect “just in case” data.

exercises.question: Explain why pseudonymisation is not the same as anonymisation.
exercises.answer: Pseudonymisation replaces direct identifiers with codes, but a separately held key or other information may allow re-linkage; it remains personal data under many regimes. Anonymisation aims to make identification no longer reasonably likely, considering singling out, linkage and auxiliary information. Removing names alone is not anonymisation. Legal classification and safeguards require contextual assessment.

exercises.question: Write an incident escalation checklist for a misdirected spreadsheet containing sensitive records.
exercises.answer: Incident checklist: stop further sharing; do not delete evidence; notify designated privacy/security contact immediately; record what was sent, to whom, when, where and which fields; preserve logs; request recipient containment through approved channel; do not independently investigate beyond role; follow breach assessment and notification process; document remediation and lessons. Never conceal an incident or forward the file to more people while trying to fix it.

title: Career progression and specialization
learning_outcomes: Compare specialist and leadership pathways in healthcare analytics.
Identify the additional competencies required for progression beyond entry-level reporting.
Build a skill roadmap aligned with a chosen specialisation.
Use evidence, feedback and project outcomes to guide development.
Maintain domain knowledge while adapting to evolving tools.

blocks.text: Progression usually requires reliable ownership, sound judgement, stakeholder trust and measurable delivery. Add new tools when they solve a defined problem, not merely because they are fashionable.

RWE adds causal inference, observational study design, claims/EHR data and regulatory evidence standards. Pharmacovigilance adds case processing, coding, signal detection and safety governance. Clinical informatics adds workflow, terminology, interoperability and implementation.

Analytics engineering adds robust SQL, dimensional modelling, orchestration, testing and data platform practices. Data science adds advanced statistics, machine learning, validation and model governance. Cloud engineering adds infrastructure, security, deployment and operations.

Senior analysts and leads set standards, mentor others, manage stakeholder expectations, prioritise work and own quality. Leadership requires communication and accountability, not only technical depth.
Maintain a skills matrix, quarterly goals, portfolio updates and feedback log. Review role requirements periodically and replace outdated learning priorities with evidence from actual work.

blocks.label: Same professional outcome
blocks.text: The professional deliverable must be reproducible on Linux and Windows. Use the appropriate shell and application route; do not paste commands from one shell into another.

Linux: use your normal user account and protect private application documents with appropriate directory permissions. Windows: use an access-controlled user folder and review sharing/sync settings. For both systems, use a private repository or local-only storage for personal application records; do not commit identity documents, recruiter correspondence containing personal data, passwords or client data.

Portable workflow: keep templates in Markdown, CSV and plain text where possible; use UTF-8; avoid absolute paths; use Git for versioned public portfolio code, not private job-search records. For Python tools, use pathlib and a project virtual environment. Verify the same files and outputs on both OSs.

Verification: record the OS, shell, application version, source file, output file and a short acceptance check. When a GUI application differs by platform, document the equivalent deliverable rather than claiming identical menus or features.

items: Wrong shell syntax: confirm whether the terminal is Bash, Fish, PowerShell or CMD before running a command.
File sync or permissions: verify the folder is private and that public sharing is disabled before storing application or client records.
Git accidentally stages private files: inspect `git status` and `git diff --cached`; unstage sensitive files before committing and rotate any exposed credentials.
Different document formatting: export a PDF copy for review and inspect the final rendered output before sending.
Unclear requirements: stop and clarify scope, authority, data permissions, deadline and acceptance criteria rather than guessing.

blocks.text: Save the completed exercise, a short explanation of decisions, validation evidence and a reflection on what you would improve. For portfolio work, use synthetic data and public-safe examples. For job-search work, keep private records out of public repositories.

blocks.label: Integrity rule
blocks.text: Never invent employment, credentials, project impact, clinical outcomes, client references or tool proficiency. Explain what you did, what you learned and what remains untested.

exercises.question: Choose one specialisation and map five competency gaps with practical evidence for each.
exercises.answer: Choose one specialisation (for example clinical data analytics) and list five measurable gaps: advanced SQL, clinical terminology/data models, longitudinal cohort design, BI semantic modelling and governance. For each gap define a practical artifact, assessment criterion, mentor/reviewer and due date. Avoid selecting several specialisations simultaneously. Reassess after completing a project and comparing current vacancies.

exercises.question: Design a 12-month development plan with quarterly deliverables and a review method.
exercises.answer: Quarterly plan example: Q1 strengthen SQL and data quality with tested queries; Q2 build a reproducible clinical cohort analysis; Q3 develop a governed dashboard and stakeholder presentation; Q4 lead an end-to-end capstone and conduct peer review. Review every quarter using completed deliverables, quality defects, stakeholder feedback and job requirements. Adjust scope when work or study commitments change.

exercises.question: Compare analytics engineer, RWE analyst and clinical informatics pathways.
exercises.answer: Analytics engineer focuses on reliable data models, transformation pipelines, testing and analytics infrastructure. RWE analyst focuses on observational study design, epidemiology, confounding, healthcare data and evidence generation. Clinical informatics focuses on clinical workflows, information systems, terminology and safe implementation. Compare daily tasks, methods, required domain depth and entry-level evidence rather than relying on job titles alone.

exercises.question: Write a promotion-readiness evidence log using project ownership, quality and stakeholder outcomes.
exercises.answer: Promotion evidence log: project ownership and scope; quality and reliability improvements; reproducible deliverables; stakeholder decisions supported; communication and mentoring; governance compliance; measurable outcomes with a clear baseline; and feedback. Separate individual contribution from team results. Avoid unsupported revenue or patient-outcome claims. Promotion readiness is determined by employer expectations, not a self-assigned title.

title: Final professional readiness assessment
learning_outcomes: Evaluate readiness across technical, healthcare-domain, communication and professional-practice competencies.
Complete an integrated practical assessment using synthetic data.
Defend methodology, validation, metric definitions and limitations.
Present a portfolio case study and respond to interview questions.
Create a realistic next-step plan based on demonstrated gaps.

blocks.text: Readiness is not a feeling or a certificate count. It is demonstrated ability to complete tasks accurately, explain choices, document limitations and ask for help when outside scope.

The assessment should include data inspection, SQL or spreadsheet transformation, Python/R analysis, a metric definition, a visual, a written interpretation and a reproducible handoff. Use synthetic data and a defined time limit.
Explain the question, data grain, cohort, cleaning, validation, method, denominator, result, uncertainty, limitation and next action. Be prepared to show the actual code and reproduce a result.
Complete one technical interview, one behavioural interview and one stakeholder case. Score correctness, reasoning, communication, honesty, time management and safety judgement.

Classify gaps as critical, important or optional. Assign each a practical task, deadline, evidence and review date. Apply to suitable roles while continuing to learn; do not wait for imaginary perfection.

exercises.question: Complete the final assessment rubric and attach evidence for each competency.
exercises.answer: Complete a rubric with competency, evidence link, reviewer, result, gap and next action. Attach actual files or repository paths for Excel, SQL, Python/R, statistics, healthcare interpretation, data quality, communication, reproducibility and privacy. Mark missing evidence as “not demonstrated”; do not award yourself full credit for course attendance. A reviewer should be able to reproduce the work from the README.

exercises.question: Deliver a 10-minute portfolio presentation and answer five challenge questions.
exercises.answer: A 10-minute portfolio presentation: 1 minute problem and audience; 1 minute data provenance and cohort; 2 minutes methods; 2 minutes validation; 2 minutes findings and visualisation; 1 minute limitations and governance; 1 minute next steps. Prepare challenge questions on denominator, missingness, bias, leakage, uncertainty and reproducibility. Never expose PHI or imply a synthetic capstone was used in live clinical care.

exercises.question: Complete a timed SQL/Python/statistics exercise and record errors and corrections.
exercises.answer: Timed assessment should include SQL joins/aggregation/window functions, a Python quality audit, and interpretation of descriptive statistics or a confidence interval. Record start/end time, correct outputs, errors, debugging steps and final rerun. Evaluate reasoning and validation, not speed alone. Use a clean dataset copy and compare outputs against an answer key. If a result differs, trace the denominator and transformation before changing code.

exercises.question: Create a 30-day career action plan with applications, portfolio improvements and mock interview practice.
exercises.answer: A 30-day plan should set weekly targets: improve one portfolio defect, complete one timed SQL/Python/statistics practice, submit a small number of eligible tailored applications, conduct one mock interview, and review feedback. Track application quality and evidence gaps rather than applying indiscriminately. Include restudy time and a weekly review. No plan guarantees an offer; adjust based on actual vacancy requirements and feedback.
